title: Members on books, reviews and short stories · AquaTerra
description: Book reviews, short stories and personal reading essays by AquaTerra members, including White Nights and Vibe Reviewing, from Groundwork Diaries.
lede: AquaTerra's members write about what they read: a short story that sat on a to-read list for a long time, a room of shelves full of very different books, and a piece about a friendship that is still missed. This page is a reading guide to those pieces, and it links to Book Basket, where our students collect old books for kids who need them.

sections.heading: reviews and short reads
body: White Nights is the closest thing here to a book review. The member writes that the story had sat on their to-be-read list for a long time before it blew up on BookTok, and that at under a hundred pages it was the right palate cleanser between longer books. The review is mostly about how glad they were to finally pick it up.

Vibe Reviewing takes a different route. It opens in a room of shelves, with collections that run from the King James Bible to The Mortal Instruments, and from Dickens to Riordan, Plato to Tolkien. The room and the mix of books in it come first, before any single book is judged.

sections.heading: the feelings that come with reading
body: The Art of Nostalgia and Heartbreak is a personal piece about missing a friendship. It opens at four in the morning, with a coffee and the thought of an old best friend, and it stays with that feeling of a loss that never quite goes away. Reading pieces like this is a reminder that the best writing here is often about ordinary hours.

People in the Mirror looks back at the writer as a child, when they brought a Barbie everywhere, even to the bathroom, and the world could wait. Ungrateful Much is a shorter essay about people who take time, kindness and support and never say thank you. Both pieces ask the reader to notice how people change, and how they treat each other along the way.

sections.heading: where to start
body: For a quick read, start with White Nights, then Vibe Reviewing. For something slower and more personal, The Art of Nostalgia and Heartbreak and People in the Mirror are closer to memoir. Before you Judge Read This and Cup of Tea are short stories about everyday moments: a cab ride across the city, and an afternoon in Patna.

Reading also runs into the work we do. Book Basket collects old books across Kolkata and sets them aside for underprivileged children, and the [Book Basket page](/impact/book-basket) lists where those drives went. If you want to share your own reading with younger kids, [how to run a reading session for kids](/impact/how-to-run-a-reading-session-for-kids) explains how our teams do it.

learnings: A short book can be the right next read when a longer one has been hard to finish.
A good review describes the feeling a book leaves behind, as well as what happens in it.
A viral post can move a book to the top of a long to-read list, as it did for one member.
Small moments, a four in the morning coffee or a child with a Barbie, carry more feeling than a summary of events.

faqs.q: Where can I read book reviews written by teenagers in Kolkata?
faqs.a: AquaTerra members write book reviews, short stories and personal reading essays on Groundwork Diaries, the students' writing on this site. White Nights and Vibe Reviewing are among the reviews and reading pieces there.

faqs.q: Does AquaTerra publish short stories written by students?
faqs.a: Yes. Some of the member writing on Groundwork Diaries is short fiction, such as Cup of Tea, which is set in Patna, and Before you Judge Read This, which takes place during a cab ride across the city.

faqs.q: What is White Nights about, according to the AquaTerra member who wrote it up?
faqs.a: The member says the short story had been on their to-be-read list for a long time before it blew up on BookTok. At under a hundred pages it was a quick read, and they say they were glad to finally pick it up.

faqs.q: What does Book Basket do with the books it collects?
faqs.a: Book Basket collects old books across Kolkata and sets them aside for underprivileged children. AquaTerra's students run each collection, and the series has its own page in the [impact library](/impact/book-basket).

faqs.q: How do I join AquaTerra if I love reading?
faqs.a: AquaTerra is a free, student-run registered charitable trust for members aged 14 to 19. Join by signing in with Google and waiting for an approval, then take part in drives such as Book Basket. [Join AquaTerra](/join) to start.
